title: OpenHOI: Open-World Hand-Object Interaction Synthesis with Multimodal Large

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.1 (Dataset) and corresponding claims in Abstract, Introduction, and Results
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims to synthesize HOI for 'unseen objects' and 'open-world' scenarios, but explicitly states: 'the unseen testing set includes object instances and categories potentially overlapping with training, limiting strict unseen generalization claims.' This undermines the main claim of open-world generalization and indicates the experimental protocol does not properly isolate truly unseen objects, inflating the reported 'unseen' performance.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix C.2 (Tables A2 and A3) and nowhere else defined
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Metrics 'Physical realism ↑' and 'IV ↓' are used in Tables A2 and A3 to compare models and perform ablations, but they are never defined anywhere in the main paper or appendix. No explanation of how they are computed, their range, or their units is provided, making the results uninterpretable.

The text says: 'The backbone is a ReCon++ [34] network (or a similar architecture)...'. However, reference [34] is ShapeLLM (Qi et al., 2024), not ReCon++. The correct citation for ReCon++ is the 'Contrast with Reconstruct' paper by Qi et al., which appears as reference [33] in the bibliography.

The term 'In-context 3D Affordance Reasoning' is misleading. The described method fine-tunes a multimodal large language model with added segmentation tokens and supervised losses to predict affordance maps from object point clouds and instruction text. This is standard supervised learning, not in-context learning (where a model performs a task from a few demonstrations without parameter updates). Using 'in-context' falsely suggests a different learning paradigm.

The sentence states: '...freezing its 3D encoder and augmenting the visual backbone with Uni3D for robust dense 3D prediction...'. Uni3D is introduced without any citation or reference. A careful reviewer would demand a proper citation for this component; its origin and technical details are not provided.
